symptom: `create odata client` with credentials given as constants (`HttpUsername: '@Module.ApiUser'`) still gets HTTP 401 and an empty client, after the fix that made literal credentials work. Sharpened by the same release making a constant `ServiceUrl` mandatory — the shape the tool insists on is the shape whose credentials it will not read
cause: `resolveCredential` trusted the visitor's isLiteral flag. `'@Module.ApiUser'` **is** a STRING_LITERAL, so the flag said "literal" and the previous code sent the fifteen characters `@Module.ApiUser` as the username — and the unresolved-credential note did not fire either, because as far as the code knew nothing was unresolved
insight: **A syntactic classification is not a semantic one.** The visitor can say "this was a quoted string"; only the executor can say "this quoted string names a constant". Any flag of the form isLiteral needs the consumer to ask what the literal *contains* before treating it as a value. **The fix is to resolve, not to refuse**: a constant's design-time default is exactly what Studio Pro sends on the same fetch, so reading it is the value rather than a workaround — and mxcli already has the project open. Three spellings must all work (`'v'`, `@M.C`, `'@M.C'`); a dotted literal like a password containing a dot must not be mistaken for a reference. Tests `cmd_odata_metadata_auth_test.go`. mxcli-formula1 #23 follow-up
